Literature-informed assessment: The statement is consistent with flexible inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford, 2005) and a forward-looking, inertial Taylor-type rule (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), evidenced by “symmetric” 2% language, close monitoring of inflation, and guidance that the funds rate will remain below its longer-run level “for some time.” The decision to begin balance-sheet normalization while keeping the policy rate unchanged embodies gradualism and interest-rate smoothing typical in estimated policy rules, supporting financial conditions while modestly lifting term premia; the literature cited notes QE’s limited effect on growth, so its unwind should be only mildly restrictive. Hurricanes’ temporary energy-price effects fit cost-push shocks that New Keynesian/“cost channel” studies (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005; Ravenna and Walsh, 2006) advise not to overreact to, reinforcing the Committee’s medium-term focus. With solid job gains and firmer business investment (consistent with financial-accelerator channels, e.g., Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist) offset by persistent sub-2% inflation, the tone is cautiously constructive. Netting these elements yields a mildly positive sentiment, slightly above neutral.
